steps.title: Independent checks

steps.title: Identify the noun’s case role
steps.body: In the supplied Муж говорит, the husband is the subject and the talking verb states its action. The subject noun is nominative. Recognizing the English sentence meaning is useful, but the role check asks whether the noun is a subject or direct object. Do not guess nominative merely because a case is unfamiliar.

steps.title: Separate the subject from its description
steps.body: In Поезд старый, the train is the subject noun and old is its predicate description. This present property clause has no overt Russian copula. The noun’s case role is nominative subject, not accusative direct object. A dictionary-looking noun or familiar translation alone does not identify its role in every construction.

steps.title: Apply the distinction to a different supplied noun
steps.body: Студент новый supplies a second independent property clause: the student is the subject noun, and new describes that subject. Its case role is nominative subject. Keep Муж говорит — The husband is talking and Поезд старый — The train is old as correct sentence meanings; the optional reference choices do not demonstrate this case role. These supplied examples are deliberately taught, not unseen evidence or unrestricted productive case use. Other constructions have nominative predicate nouns; not every nominative noun is a subject.

items.prompt: Which case role does the noun naming the husband have in this supplied clause?
options: The noun names the subject, in the nominative case.
The noun names a direct object, in the accusative case.
items.answer: The noun names the subject, in the nominative case.
items.feedback: In this supplied clause, the husband is the subject that the sentence makes a statement about. Its case role is nominative subject. The talking verb reports its action. The direct-object explanation does not describe this noun here. Knowing the English translation alone does not answer the requested role. Other constructions can use nominative predicate nouns; do not assume every nominative noun is a subject.
distractorRationales: The requested noun is the subject here; the clause does not present it as a direct object.

distractorDifference: The requested noun is the subject here; the clause does not present it as a direct object.
